checks.name: STEP 1: Apache service active
checks.solution:
Start Apache: sudo systemctl start apache2
Enable on boot: sudo systemctl enable apache2
Check logs: sudo journalctl -xe | grep apache

checks.name: STEP 2: Apache rewrite module enabled
checks.solution: Enable the module: sudo a2enmod rewrite && sudo systemctl restart apache2

checks.name: STEP 3: Apache headers module enabled
checks.solution: Enable the module: sudo a2enmod headers && sudo systemctl restart apache2

checks.name: STEP 4: Apache AllowOverride All configured
checks.solution: Set AllowOverride All in /etc/apache2/apache2.conf for the /var/www/ directory block, then: sudo systemctl restart apache2

checks.name: STEP 5: Apache serving piClinic frontend
checks.solution:
Run: sudo systemctl start apache2
If it fails to start: sudo journalctl -xe | grep apache
Verify deployment: bash ~/piClinic/tools/deploy.sh v2

checks.name: STEP 6: PHP 8.4 installed
checks.solution:
PHP 8.4 is required. On Ubuntu: sudo add-apt-repository ppa:ondrej/php && sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libapache2-mod-php8.4 php8.4-common php8.4-mysql
On Pi OS Bookworm: sudo apt-get install -y libapache2-mod-php php-common php-mysql

checks.name: STEP 7: PHP mysql extension
checks.solution: Install: sudo apt-get install -y php8.4-mysql (Ubuntu) or php-mysql (Pi)

checks.name: STEP 8: PHP mbstring extension
checks.solution: Install: sudo apt-get install -y php8.4-mbstring (Ubuntu) or php-mbstring (Pi)

checks.name: STEP 9: PHP curl extension
checks.solution: Install: sudo apt-get install -y php8.4-curl (Ubuntu) or php-curl (Pi)

checks.name: STEP 10: PHP zip extension
checks.solution: Install: sudo apt-get install -y php8.4-zip (Ubuntu) or php-zip (Pi)

checks.name: STEP 11: PHP display_errors On (Apache)
checks.target: curl -sf http://localhost/phpinfo.php | grep -o 'display_errorsOnOn'
checks.solution:
Set display_errors = On in the Apache php.ini.
Find the path: php --ini | grep 'Loaded Configuration' | sed 's|/cli/|/apache2/|'
Then: sudo systemctl restart apache2
Note: phpinfo.php must be present at /var/www/html/phpinfo.php

checks.name: STEP 12: PHP timezone configured (Apache)
checks.solution:
Set date.timezone in the Apache php.ini (find path: php --ini | sed 's|/cli/|/apache2/|')
Example: date.timezone = America/New_York
Then: sudo systemctl restart apache2

checks.name: STEP 13: PHP memory_limit 512M (Apache)
checks.solution:
Set memory_limit = 512M in the Apache php.ini
Find path: php --ini | grep 'Loaded Configuration' | sed 's|/cli/|/apache2/|'
Then: sudo systemctl restart apache2

checks.name: STEP 14: clinic group exists
checks.solution: Create the group: sudo groupadd clinic

checks.name: STEP 15: clinic user exists
checks.solution: Create the user: sudo useradd clinic -g clinic && sudo mkdir -p /home/clinic && sudo chown clinic /home/clinic

checks.name: STEP 16: MariaDB service active
checks.solution:
Start MariaDB: sudo systemctl start mariadb
Enable on boot: sudo systemctl enable mariadb

checks.name: STEP 17: MariaDB admin connectivity
checks.solution:
If authentication fails, check the DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD set in piclinic_setup.conf.
If the admin user does not exist, check STEP 7 of the setup script ran successfully.

checks.name: STEP 18: piclinic database exists
checks.solution:
Load the schema: cd ~/piClinic/sql && mariadb -u admin -p<password> piclinic < piclinic.sql
If the database does not exist, re-run STEP 13 of the setup script.

checks.name: STEP 19: CTS-user account exists
checks.target: mariadb -u admin -p${MYSQL_PASSWORD} -e "SELECT User FROM mysql.user WHERE User='CTS-user';"
checks.solution:
Create the CTS-user account by re-running STEP 13 of the setup script, or manually:
  cp ~/piClinic/sql/create_dbuser*.sql ~/ && sed -i 's/YOURPASSWORD/<password>/g' ~/create_dbuser*.sql
  sudo mariadb -u root < ~/create_dbuser*.sql

checks.name: STEP 20: Composer installed
checks.solution:
Install Composer per STEP 8 of the setup script:
  php -r "copy('https://getcomposer.org/installer', 'composer-setup.php');"
  sudo php composer-setup.php --install-dir=/usr/local/bin --filename=composer
  rm composer-setup.php

checks.name: STEP 21: Node.js 20.x installed
checks.solution:
Node.js 20 LTS is required. Install via NodeSource:
  curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | sudo -E bash -
  sudo apt-get install -y nodejs

checks.name: STEP 22: npm installed
checks.solution: npm is normally installed with Node. Reinstall Node via NodeSource per STEP 9 of the setup script.

checks.name: STEP 23: PHPUnit 13.x installed
checks.solution:
Install PHPUnit 13.x globally (required for PHP 8.4):
  sudo wget -O /usr/local/bin/phpunit https://phar.phpunit.de/phpunit-13.phar
  sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/phpunit

checks.name: STEP 24: piClinic repository present
checks.solution: Clone the repository: git clone -b main_v2 https://github.com/rbwatson/piClinic ~/piClinic

checks.name: STEP 25: /var/local/piclinic owned by www-data
checks.solution: Fix ownership: sudo chown -R www-data:www-data /var/local/piclinic

checks.name: STEP 26: /var/log/piclinic directory present
checks.solution:
Create the log directory:
  sudo mkdir -p /var/log/piclinic
  sudo chown www-data:www-data /var/log/piclinic
  sudo chmod 770 /var/log/piclinic

checks.name: STEP 27: piclinic schema tables present
checks.solution:
Load the schema: cd ~/piClinic/sql && mariadb -u admin -p<password> piclinic < piclinic.sql
Load ICD-10 data: mariadb -u admin -p<password> piclinic < icd10.sql

checks.name: STEP 28: icd10 table populated
checks.target: mariadb -u admin -p${MYSQL_PASSWORD} piclinic -e "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM icd10;" 2>/dev/null
checks.solution: Load ICD-10 data: cd ~/piClinic/sql && mariadb -u admin -p<password> piclinic < icd10.sql

checks.name: STEP 29: v2 API .env file deployed
checks.solution:
Deploy the v2 API: cd ~/piClinic && bash tools/deploy.sh v2
Then configure the .env file: sudo nano /var/www/html/api/.env

checks.name: STEP 30: v2 vendor directory deployed
checks.solution:
Deploy the v2 API: cd ~/piClinic && bash tools/deploy.sh v2
This runs composer install automatically.
